subject.title: enhancement: Optimize voice message processing pipeline for Telegram

question: What Telegram voice pipeline contract should OpenClaw support before implementation: narrow feedback fixes, async/background TTS delivery, voice-priority queuing, or a full staged STT/TTS pipeline with state snapshots?
rationale: The request crosses Telegram ingress ordering, audio preflight, provider streaming support, TTS delivery, cache policy, and session-state semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Design staged async STT/TTS pipeline
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker and require a maintainer-approved design with timing snapshots, ordering guarantees, cache rules, and live Telegram benchmarks before implementation.

options.title: Limit near-term scope to narrow UX slices
options.body: Handle https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58887, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42539, and telemetry as separate smaller items while deferring the larger queue/streaming rewrite.

options.title: Reject broad pipeline work for now
options.body: Close the broad rewrite direction and direct users to existing Talk, provider, and TTS tuning surfaces until stronger live performance evidence is available.

recommendation.title: Design staged async STT/TTS pipeline
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker and require a maintainer-approved design with timing snapshots, ordering guarantees, cache rules, and live Telegram benchmarks before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans TTS core, Telegram processing, and product-level delivery semantics, where the strongest combined history points to this owner path.
